title: 04 Assemble the archive package for NCEI
text:
Status
The package layout below is a proposal to agree with NCEI and with Matt Biddle and Enrique Montes, who are already working on NCEI publication of EcoTaxa data (the SECOORA LOI also names FathomNet in that work). It is BagIt-style because a checksummed, self-describing bag survives any transport. Which route NCEI prefers (Send2NCEI for a one-off, ATRAC with a submission agreement for a recurring flow, or a FathomNet-mediated path) and which metadata profile the imaging pipeline requires are the first questions for them; nothing here is an NCEI decision, and nothing here submits.

title: 04 Assemble the archive package for NCEI
section: What a submission would then look like (assumption, to agree)
text:
What a submission would then look like (assumption, to agree)

Copy the bag to the staging bucket (egress-free object storage; a public copy via NODD if NOAA wants one), under ecotaxa/{dataset_key}/{version}/.
Send NCEI the bag’s location and bag-info.txt through the agreed route (S2N for a pilot; ATRAC with a submission agreement for the recurring flow). The ISO 19115-2 record NCEI needs would be generated from the same EML with NCEI’s template once the profile is agreed; data/metadata/dataset.json holds the ACDD-style attributes it would draw on.
On accession, write the accession number and DOI back into the project’s EML, so the next DwC-A version cites the archived copy.
A re-validation or a new cruise makes a new version; a submitted version is never edited.

title: 04 Assemble the archive package for NCEI
text:
Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)

Scale. Project 4’s bag is 10.05 GB, 967,734 images and 967,842 payload files; build, manifest and verify (ok) take 12 minutes on the mini. Two loops that were fine on eight objects were not: copying one image per call (now one vectorized file.copy), and ncei_verify() looking each manifest entry up by name inside a loop, which is quadratic and ran for over half an hour without finishing (now one vectorized comparison; a test covers missing, unlisted and changed files together).
Spotlight on macOS indexes every new image and competes for the CPU; data/.metadata_never_index (made by scripts/render_project.sh) keeps it off.
One image per object: exporting with with_images = "first" is what removed the duplicate second images of the Ifremer backup; an "all" export would bring them back into the bag.
Print counts and the first lines, never a million-line listing, into a rendered page.

title: 02 Categories to WoRMS
text:
EcoTaxa’s taxonomy is WoRMS now
Since its 2026 major version EcoTaxa uses the WoRMS taxonomy: every phylogenetic category carries an AphiaID and a WoRMS lineage, deprecated categories were remapped (Ifremer publishes the list), and the API has a taxon_set/wormsification call that maps any category, morphological ones included, to its nearest WoRMS taxon. The TSV export still carries the category’s name, EcoTaxa id and lineage rather than the AphiaID, so this notebook resolves each distinct category once, through the node’s taxonomy, into a table a person can review. EcoTaxa’s own mapping is shown beside the decision as a cross-check.

title: 02 Categories to WoRMS
text:
Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)

73 categories in use: 48 resolve directly to an AphiaID, 10 to their nearest WoRMS ancestor, 15 are excluded, none unresolved. The ancestor rows are the ones a taxonomist should read first (for project 4, tintinnida to Tintinnidae, centric to Bacillariophyta, ciliate-tintinnids to Ciliophora).
Exclusions decide most of what reaches OBIS: of 15,788 validated objects, 11,927 sit in excluded categories (rods<other 4,082, artefact 3,043, ghost, dubious, detritus, unidentified cells), so only 3,861 become occurrences. A morphological category like rods<other is a question for the data owner, not a rule to change silently.
Keep one lookup per project (metadata/taxa_lookup_project-<id>.csv): the same category can be reviewed differently for two instruments.

This site is the companion to the brief US EcoTaxa: pipelines to OBIS and NCEI (6 November 2026, a Word document kept with the proposal files). title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
The notebooks



Notebook
What it does
Reusable logic




01 Export
pulls the project through the REST API (token login, general export job, TSV + images), caches it under data/
R/ecotaxa_api.R


02 Taxa
resolves every EcoTaxa category to WoRMS into a reviewable lookup table, with explicit rules for non-living and morphological categories
R/taxa.R


03 OBIS
builds Event, Occurrence and eMoF, the EML and meta.xml, zips a Darwin Core Archive, validates it (obistools)
R/dwc.R, R/eml.R


04 NCEI
assembles a BagIt-style archive package (images, TSV, DwC-A, metadata, SHA-256 manifest) and verifies it; describes the submission route as a proposal
R/ncei.R



Every rule in R/ has a testthat test on a small synthetic fixture (tests/testthat/); run them with Rscript tests/run_tests.R. The notebooks call the functions, the tests assert them, so the two cannot drift.

title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
Where it comes from
The structure borrows from the CalCOFI Darwin Core pipeline (publish notebooks, calcofi4db): a term map that drives meta.xml so a column without a term is an error; vocabulary ids filled only on an exact match, never invented; deterministic archives with a content hash; and findings that gate the build instead of warnings that scroll by.

title: EcoTaxa to OBIS and NCEI: a working demo
text:
Honest limits of the demo

The demo project’s eight objects are all predicted by the classifier, none validated. The OBIS notebook therefore opts in to predicted objects (include_predicted = TRUE) and the archive carries identificationVerificationStatus = predicted on every occurrence. A real publication would not.
EcoTaxa’s taxonomy is WoRMS since its 2026 major version, so the two phylogenetic categories (Cyclopoida, Oncaeidae) carry an AphiaID and publish. The four morphological ones (detritus, other, egg, t001) are excluded by rule; EcoTaxa’s own mapping would publish egg and other as Biota and drop the other two (notebook 02 shows the cross-check).
The NERC P01 ids in metadata/measurement_type.csv are filled only where the concept is exact; most are empty on purpose and show up as no_measurement_type_id warnings.
The NCEI package layout and route are a proposal to agree with NCEI, not an NCEI specification.

title: 01 Export a project from EcoTaxa
text:
What this does
EcoTaxa’s REST API ({ECOTAXA_URL}/api/docs) exposes a general export job: it writes a zip with one TSV per sample (object, sample, acquisition and process fields, plus each object’s category, annotation status, annotator and date) and, optionally, the images. This notebook logs in with a token, starts the job for the project, waits for it, downloads and unzips it under data/export/, and reads the TSVs into one objects table cached as Parquet. Later notebooks read the cache and never touch the node.
The project is ECOTAXA_PROJECT_ID (default 2, the demo project; the setup below prints which one this page ran on). Credentials come from a git-ignored .Renviron (ECOTAXA_URL, ECOTAXA_USER, ECOTAXA_PASSWORD) or from ECOTAXA_TOKEN, a login token handed to the render so no password sits on the machine. An export already unzipped under data/export/ is reused unless ECOTAXA_REFRESH=1. When no login is configured on project 2, the notebook falls back to the upstream test set in data-raw/import_test/, which is the byte-identical source of project 2’s eight objects (see data-raw/README.md), so the rest of the pipeline still runs on the same data; it says so below.

Notes

title: 01 Export a project from EcoTaxa
text:
Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)
The first real export, of 967,734 objects, found five things the eight-object demo could not. Each is now handled in R/ecotaxa_api.R or R/taxa.R, with a test:



What happened
Cause
Now




422 Unprocessable Entity on starting the job
split_by = "" is not in the node’s enum (sample, acquisition, taxon, none)
ecotaxa_export_body() checks against the OpenAPI enums


500, relation "taxo_recast" does not exist
the node’s DB was built without two tables (a node issue, not a pipeline one)
fixed on the node; see 05 Migrate


the job sat at “1 % Start TSV export” forever
the back end was OOM-killed (2.44 GB container) loading every row at once; the job row is never updated after that
one job per batch of samples, at most max_objects (40,000) each; a job whose progress stalls for 20 min stops the run


object_annotation_category_id missing
the export carries internal ids only with with_internal_ids
the id is resolved from the category’s display name (unique on a node) against the project’s own categories; no match stops


every date blank downstream
the export writes YYYY-MM-DD and HH:MM:SS, the import format is YYYYMMDD and HHMMSS
ecotaxa_datetime() reads both



Also: download with a long timeout and unzip with the system unzip (zip64, over 4 GB); batches leave a marker under data/export/project-<id>/batches/, so a stopped run resumes after the last finished batch; each finished job is deleted on the node so its files do not fill the node’s disk. For project 4 the 28 batches took 44 minutes and gave 105 TSVs and exactly one image per object (967,734), which also removed the 6,962 byte-identical second images the backup carried.

title: 03 Build and validate the Darwin Core Archive for OBIS
text:
Lessons learned (project 4, 2026-11-10)

Positions of 0,0 are the usual placeholder for “unknown” (project 4’s ws21093_MR_64um): dwc_event() now publishes them as no coordinates, the same rule as the sample map. A latitude or a longitude of 0 alone is kept.
Validated only by default: INCLUDE_PREDICTED turns on only when a project has no validated object (the demo); project 4’s 951,833 predictions stay out.
Column names differ by instrument. The eMoF reads sample_tot_vol (Zooscan) and object_esd; a PlanktoScope export has sample_total_volume, sample_concentrated_sample_volume, sample_dilution_factor and object_equivalent_diameter (pixels, with process_pixel). Volume, concentration and size are therefore absent for project 4 until the owner confirms units and meaning; the mapping belongs in metadata/, not guessed in code.
Child events have no coordinates: occurrences on acquisition events (738 for project 4) carry the no_coordinates warning; OBIS is expected to take them from the parent sample event, to confirm.
Metadata per project comes from metadata/projects.csv; a project without a row stops the build rather than borrowing the demo’s text or license.

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
text:
1. Fetch and unpack the backup
The owner’s “backup” export from the source node is a zip of one TSV per sample plus the images, in the import format. For project 4: export__BAK_11310_20260616_1243.zip, 8.5 GB, shared on Drive by Matt Biddle.


Code
scripts/fetch_backup.sh 1dXWk_uKw-C9eahfdDKfIndI1gLv9SiEv bak_11310


Check the disk first: the zip and its unzipped copy were about 18 GB on a /share at 90 %. Keep both until the import is verified, then delete both.

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
section: 2. Create the project, import, credit the annotators
text:
2. Create the project, import, credit the annotators


Code
A='python3 -I - '; S=scripts/node/ecotaxa_admin.py
ssh msens "$A create-project --title 'SFER MBON PlanktoScope (migrated from EcoTaxa 11310)' \
  --instrument PlanktoScope --access 1 --manager-id 5 --contact-id 5" < $S   # 5 = Enrique's account
ssh msens "$A import --project 4 --source bak_11310/unzipped" < $S          # path relative to /file_srv
ssh msens "$A job --id 2 --wait" < $S                                       # about 3 h for project 4



Owner. EcoTaxa has no “owner” role: the owner is a project manager and the contact person. Their account must exist first (it did not at first; check GET /users/search rather than trusting memory).
Annotators. The import maps annotators by name or email. Five who had no account on this node were created as inactive placeholders (status 0, a random password nobody keeps) so their validations stay credited, rather than reassigned to the owner:



Code
# scripts/node/users_<project>.csv, git-ignored: name,email[,organisation,country,reason]
scp scripts/node/users_prj4.csv msens:/tmp/ && \
  ssh msens "$A users --csv /tmp/users_prj4.csv && rm /tmp/users_prj4.csv" < $S



Access. 1 (“public”) still asks for a login; 2 (“open”) lets anyone read without one, and only members annotate or manage. Project 4 is open for link-only viewing by the group:



Code
ssh msens "$A set-access --project 4 --access 2" < $S
ssh msens "$A verify --project 4" < $S

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
text:
3. Check the node before exporting
A node built with manage.py build can lack tables: it creates only the tables of model modules that happen to be imported, and stamps no alembic version. On msens1 taxo_recast and projects_variables were missing, so every general export failed. Compare first; it is read-only:


Code
ssh msens 'docker exec -i -w /app ecotaxa-back python3 -' < scripts/node/schema_diff.py


An empty report, or only three modify_nullable lines on the *_old_2_new primary keys, is a match. If tables are missing, bring the DB forward, old to new, with each missing migration’s own SQL (alembic upgrade --sql <prev>:<rev> inside ecotaxa-back), then alembic stamp head and the upstream operator step alembic upgrade head, which should then have nothing to do. Back up with pg_dump -Fc first. scripts/node/2026-11-10_schema_to_head.sql is the record of the 2026-11-10 fix and its runbook; do not re-run it on a DB that already has the tables.

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
text:
4. Run notebooks 01–04 on the project


Code
scripts/launch_project.sh 4          # all four; or `scripts/launch_project.sh 4 04` to redo only 04
ssh macmini 'tail -f ~/Github/oceanmetrics/ecotaxa-demo/data/run_project-4.log'


The render writes _site_project-4/ on the mini, which quarto publish (from _site/) never uploads: a project’s pages are published only on purpose. Before a project’s first run, add its row to metadata/projects.csv (title, abstract, license, contact, organization) and expect notebook 02 to write metadata/taxa_lookup_project-<id>.csv for review.

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
text:
5. Share the packages for review
The packages went to the group, not to a portal: a Drive subfolder shared as viewer with the email thread, uploaded from the mini (which has the same rclone remotes as the laptop). The NCEI bag is zipped without compression (zip -0): the images are JPEGs already.


Code
cd data && zip -0 -r -q share_project-4/ecotaxa-om-prj4_2026-11-10_ncei-bag.zip ncei/ecotaxa-om-prj4_2026-11-10
rclone copy share_project-4 "gdrive-ecoquants:project-4 packages 2026-11-10" --drive-root-folder-id <folder id>

title: 05 Migrate a project from another EcoTaxa node
text:
6. Lessons for the next project

Run the real export early. The demo’s offline fallback hid a wrong request body; a real project surfaced it, plus four more issues (see the lessons in 01).
Size every step for a million. Batch the node’s export by samples, vectorize per-file work, and print counts, not listings (04).
Check the node’s schema once per node (and after each back-end upgrade) with schema_diff.py.
Unknowns stay unknown. 0,0 positions, volumes without units, sizes in pixels: publish nothing rather than a guess, and ask the data owner (03).
Questions for the owner go out with the run: license, missing positions, volume and size units, review of the ancestor and excluded taxa, and which organization and people to credit.
